🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum takes Plan México to APEC in Shenzhen, and Mexico chairs APEC in 2028</u>

Sheinbaum will be at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, November 17-19: keynote speaker before the APEC Business Advisory Council of more than 1,000 executives from the 21 economies, a plenary alongside Xi Jinping, and bilaterals with China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam. Her pitch is Plan México, investment that builds national production and adds value at home. "That is the vision of our Plan México and it is part of what we are going to put forward." Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard: APEC's 21 economies are about 60% of world GDP and half of global trade, and Mexico was elected unanimously to preside over it in 2028.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Who's behind "Cuando perdimos el juicio," the documentary against Mexico's judicial reform</u>

Contralínea traces the documentary to a network of NGOs and foundations: Juicio Justo, the Due Process of Law Foundation, Réplica, NYU's Rule of Law program and Germany's Konrad Adenauer Stiftung. Juicio Justo's director Laurence Pantin came out of México Evalúa, which receives US government money through the National Endowment for Democracy. The KAS ran training programs with Norma Piña's old Supreme Court and with the PAN, and lists among its Mexican partners the governments of Guanajuato and Chihuahua, "governed by María Eugenia Campos, who opened the door to the CIA." That old Court is the one where Piña voted against the Republican Austerity Law and the Asset Forfeiture Law.

🇲🇽🌱 <u>Mexico moves to cut 2,460 tons of agrochemicals and rebuild its soils</u>

Mexico's Agriculture Ministry and the UNDP are launching two five-year projects backed by more than $20 million from the Global Environment Facility: FARM+, to reduce and manage agrochemicals, and "Forjando alianzas por el océano," against water pollution. Target: 2,460 fewer tons of agrochemicals and sustainable practices on more than 839,000 hectares, centered on rural women and Indigenous producers in Chiapas, Jalisco, Oaxaca, the Yucatán Peninsula, Sinaloa and Veracruz. Agriculture Secretary Columba López says the goal is "to recover the health of the soils, reduce contaminants, protect ecosystems." Same government that wrote the ban on GM corn planting into the Constitution.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>The Chihuahua prosecutor who worked with the CIA fled to the US, and Washington is protecting him</u>

Guillermo Zuany, Chihuahua's former strategic operations and anti-kidnapping prosecutor under PAN governor Maru Campos, has fled to the United States and is under US government protection, The New York Times reports, citing Mexican and US officials. For more than six months Zuany coordinated CIA agents training Chihuahua's forces. He left after it emerged the FGR holds arrest warrants against him; his former boss, ex-state attorney general César Jáuregui, is already jailed on treason charges. Washington had reportedly revoked his visa over suspected cartel ties, then restored it after he worked with the CIA. Sheinbaum: "It's worth knowing who this person is and how he collaborates with one of the agencies of the United States."

🇲🇽⚡ <u>THE MEXICAN STATE NOW GENERATES 58.2% OF THE COUNTRY'S ELECTRICITY</u>

Energy Secretary Luz Elena González told the Senate that the state now produces 58.2% of the power fed into the national grid, up from 54% in 2024. Between 2000 and 2020, neoliberal policy cut public generation from 99% to 40%. The plan adds 32,000 megawatts this sexenio, 70% of it renewable. "The State has already recovered its prevalence in electricity generation," she said. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🌳 <u>MORELOS MOVES TO EXPROPRIATE THE FOREST A MURDERED ACTIVIST DEFENDED</u>

Morelos governor Margarita González Saravia is starting the expropriation of La Cazahuatera, almost five hectares of tropical dry forest in eastern Cuernavaca, for public use. Morena councilman and environmental activist Gabriel Rivas Ríos, 52, was murdered on November 4 after denouncing plans to build there. Developer Portenta Hábitat's "Alto Verde" project called for a housing development and towers up to 15 stories on land with 1,600 native trees. The owners get compensation. The forest stays.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>BUDGET 2027: COUNTRYSIDE +20.6%, HEALTH +11.3%, SCIENCE +13%</u>

Mexico's 10.6-trillion-peso 2027 budget is final, and the real-terms increases go where the 4T said they would: health +11.3%, education +10.7%, security +11.5%, science +13%, the countryside +20.6%. Sheinbaum also highlighted extra money for La Escuela es Nuestra, which sends funds straight to school communities for repairs, and for Semarnat. Overall spending rises 1.3% in real terms over 2026.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>AFTER 2027, MEXICO DEBATES WHO HOLDS POWER INSIDE THE INE</u>

Sheinbaum says that once the 2027 election is over, "it is worth discussing the concentration of power in the INE." She welcomed the INE's new tendering rules, which open contracts for ballot boxes, voting booths and materials to competition for the INE and the state OPLEs, since they "had no reason to be tied to a single company or two companies." Her rejected electoral reform aimed to stop party elites from picking plurinominal lawmakers, cut election costs and widen participation. A new reform "would have to be a national discussion," after next year's vote.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SALINAS PLIEGO DARED HER TO OPEN THE FOBAPROA FILES. SHEINBAUM SAID YES.</u>

Ricardo Salinas Pliego denies he profited from the 1990s bank bailout and challenged the government to make the Fobaproa files public. Sheinbaum took him at his word: opening the archive, for his case and every other, would let Mexicans see every deal struck under Fobaproa. Her account: after the 1994 crash, the bailout rescued Salinas y Rocha and cleared the way for Grupo Elektra to expand. The public is still paying. IPAB liabilities stood at 1.165 trillion pesos as of July.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>15 YEARS, 211 BILLION PESOS: THE MAN WHO RAN THE IFE-INE SUPPLIER NETWORK</u>

Edmundo Jacobo Molina ran the electoral institute's Executive Secretariat for 15 years, from the old IFE into the INE, overseeing a combined budget of 211 billion pesos. La Jornada reports that about 80% of contracts in that time went out as direct awards to a small circle of companies, including firms tied to the Hernández Casillas brothers, whose network landed 2,646 million pesos in electoral contracts. Jacobo now heads political training at Somos, the party founded by ex-INE officials. His answer: Morena is shifting the blame.
